column1: # The recall rep table (beads tla-1sh7.2 and tla-03ep.1, epics tla-1sh7 and
# TWO ROW KINDS, AND FIELD 1 IS WHICH. 160 reps over 57 of the 105 constructs
#   REP   120 reps over 37 of the 38 constructs in the four value-producing
#         families: core 16, functions-records 11, sets 9, sequences 2. The
#         answer is an expression and the grade is value equality. K008,
#         bullet-point boolean notation, has no row, and why is below the
#   SPEC  40 reps over all 20 constructs of the temporal family. The answer
#         has no value -- `WF_v(A)` is a promise about a behavior -- so it is
#         put in a machine and the machine is run. The grade is the vector of
#         exit codes. The section begins at THE SPEC ROWS further down.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal marker in field 1, so prose in
# this file can never be read as data.
# A REP ROW. Six fields, in order:
#   3  construct     K001-K105, resolving to a drill/INVENTORY.md row
#   5  prompt       English, naming none of the notation it asks for
# Read rows with awk -F'\t' or cut, never with IFS=$'\t' read.
# FIELD 5 IS THE FIELD THAT DECIDES WHETHER A REP IS A REP. It states a need
# and names none of the notation that answers it. Several reps share a
# construct on purpose and are phrased differently each time, so what gets
# retrieved is the fact rather than the sentence.
# THE GRADE IS VALUE EQUALITY, so any expression with the canonical's value
# scores 0. For most of these constructs that is the point. For the seven
# definition forms, K001 K071 K072 K073 K074 K075 K076, it is a real limit:
# each canonical is wrapped in a LET, because a bare definition is not an
# expression and scores 150, and each one returns a function or a set rather
# than a scalar so that the short way round is at least expensive. Even so,
# value equality cannot see that a definition was written. Those rows drill
# the construct; they do not gate it.

column1: # K008, bullet-point boolean notation, has no row and cannot have one here.
# The construct IS the layout: stacked /\ or \/ lines whose indentation is
# meaningful. Two things stop it. A tab-delimited row is one line, so field 6
# cannot carry the line breaks the layout is made of. And value equality
# grades the value, which is a truth value either way, so even folded onto one
# line the bulleted form and the infix form are the same answer. Measured:
# a canonical of (/\ TRUE /\ 1 = 1) = TRUE scores rc 0, exactly as the infix
# form does, so nothing distinguishes them. Grading it needs a check on the
# submitted TEXT rather than on its value.
# THE SPEC ROWS (bead tla-03ep.1, epic tla-i7uz). 40 reps, two per construct,
# over all 20 constructs of the temporal family.
# WHY THIS FAMILY NEEDED A SECOND ROW KIND. Nothing in it has a value.
# `WF_v(A)` is a promise about a behavior, `[]P` is a claim about every state
# of one, `x'` means nothing outside a step. `ASSUME Answer = Canonical` over
# any of them is not false, it is meaningless, so the whole family was 0 of 20
# SO THE ANSWER GOES IN A MACHINE AND THE MACHINE IS RUN. Field 4 names
# scaffolds rather than an environment: each is a WHOLE MODULE with a hole in
# it, under recall/env/spec/<name>.tla, with its obligations in
# recall/env/spec/<name>.cfg beside it. The runner drops the answer into the
# hole, hands the pair to TLC, and compares the exit code against field 8.
# NINE FIELDS, AND FIELD 7 IS THE SAME FIELD IT IS ON A REP ROW:
#   3  construct    K001-K105, resolving to a drill/INVENTORY.md row
#   4  scaffolds    comma-separated, each resolving to recall/env/spec/
#   5  prompt       English, naming none of the notation it asks for
#   7  requires     an ERE the raw answer has to match. Optional in the
#                   format and present on all 40 rows here; see below
#   8  expect       comma-separated exit codes, one per scaffold, in the
#                   scaffolds' own order. This is the KEY
#   9  check        OPTIONAL. fills a scaffold's __CHECK__ hole, which is
#                   where the state-graph fingerprint lives on the 12 action
# THE KEY IS A VECTOR BECAUSE ONE RUN CANNOT GRADE A PROPERTY. A property
# WEAKER than the one asked for also holds, and `[]TRUE` holds on everything.
# Two runs catch too-weak and too-strong. Measured 2026-10-17 on TLC2
# 2026.07.31.184830: even two miss a near neighbor, since `<>(level = 1)` has
# the same two-sided profile as `<>(level = 2)`, which is why S011 names four
# THE THREE HOLES, which is how 20 constructs are reached rather than four:
#   the fairness hole   S001-S008, one run, keyed on the exit code. The hole
#                       is the conjunct beside Init and the step relation
#   the property hole   S009-S026, a battery of two to four, keyed on the
#                       vector. The hole is the formula the .cfg registers
#   the action hole     S027-S040, keyed on an INVARIANT in the scaffold AND
#                       a state-graph fingerprint read through TLCGet in a
#                       POSTCONDITION. The hole is an action, a Spec body, a
#                       `vars` tuple or the VARIABLES line itself
# THE FINGERPRINT ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH AND THAT WAS MEASURED, not reasoned.
# Swapping which variable moves gives an isomorphic state graph: on act-step,
# `lamp < 1 /\ lamp' = lamp + 1 /\ level' = level` reaches 4 distinct states
# at diameter 4 exactly as the canonical does, and passes at rc 0 with the
# INVARIANT removed. The scaffold's INVARIANT names the variable that is NOT
# the prompt's, so the swap scores 12 instead.
# AND THE FINGERPRINT IS THREE NUMBERS RATHER THAN TWO FOR THE SAME REASON.
# distinct states at diameter 2. They generate 4 and 10. TLCGet("generated")
# is what separates S031 from the wider answer.
# WHY FIELD 7 IS ON EVERY ROW HERE. An exit code cannot see how a verdict was
# reached, so the construct gate carries more weight than it does on a value
# row. Measured: `<>(level = 2)` conjoined into fair-lift's fairness hole
# PASSES at rc 0. It is the goal asserted as a hypothesis rather than a
# fairness condition, and no run can tell. `\bWF_` closes it, and the refusal
# says the construct was not written, which is exactly what happened.
# TLCGet("level") IS NOT THE DEPTH. It returns 0 in a POSTCONDITION.
# TLCGet("diameter") is the depth, and TLCGet("level") cost the spike a wrong
